text: By the sheep gate in Jerusalem there was a pool called Bethesda, ringed by five covered porches.

And those porches were full of the city's most hopeless people — the blind, the lame, the paralyzed — all waiting on a legend: every so often the water stirred, and the first one in, people said, would be healed.
Imagine the math of that place.
And the fastest one wins a race for the people who can't run.
